title: Indian Hilly-Region Generalization Audit
scientific_verdict: No real Indian hilly-terrain evidence exists in the current repo. Urban-scene results are not enough to claim utility in northern-India disaster scenarios.
evidence_basis: scripts/phase55_clean_selection.py contains explicit placeholder evaluation logic and synthetic results.
scripts/phase56_forensic_verification.py independently flags the earlier metrics as non-plausible as real inference evidence.
depthwizard/depth/depth_anything.py documents that Depth Anything V2 is a relative-depth prior, not a metric terrain sensor.
depthwizard/calibration/engine.py uses geometric and morphological approximations for DTM / nDSM calibration, without Indian terrain validation.
depthwizard/analysis/slope.py separates terrain slope from facade slope, but it does not validate landslide or flood hazard modeling.
The workspace data directories are limited to dfc2019 and dfc2023_multicity; no Indian hilly benchmark is present.

minimum_justified_next_step.dataset: Create a georeferenced Indian hilly benchmark with DEM/LiDAR, slope strata, vegetation, and disaster labels.
minimum_justified_next_step.evaluation: Measure DTM/nDSM error and hazard-region performance separately from ordinary terrain.
minimum_justified_next_step.decision_rule: Only proceed to operational claims after external Indian terrain validation passes the required error and hazard metrics.

recommended_position: DepthWizard is promising as a research prototype for urban monocular elevation reconstruction, but it is not yet scientifically defensible for Indian hilly disaster management.
